questions.question: What does AM stand for in signal modulation?
questions.explanation: AM varies the amplitude of the carrier wave to encode information.

questions.question: In FM, which property of the carrier wave is varied?
questions.explanation: Frequency Modulation varies the carrier's frequency according to the signal.

questions.question: What does PM stand for in modulation techniques?
questions.explanation: Phase Modulation encodes data by shifting the phase of the carrier wave.

questions.question: Which multiplexing technique gives each signal a dedicated time slot?
questions.explanation: Time Division Multiplexing interleaves signals in separate time slots.

questions.question: Which multiplexing technique separates signals by assigning different frequency bands?
questions.explanation: Frequency Division Multiplexing divides the channel bandwidth into frequency bands.

questions.question: What does CDMA stand for?
questions.explanation: CDMA lets all users share the same band simultaneously using unique codes.

questions.question: WDM is primarily used with which transmission medium?
questions.explanation: Wavelength Division Multiplexing carries multiple light wavelengths on one fiber.

questions.question: Which cellular generation was entirely analog?
questions.explanation: 1G systems like AMPS used analog voice transmission.

questions.question: Which cellular generation first introduced digital voice and SMS?
questions.explanation: 2G (e.g., GSM) digitized voice and added text messaging.

questions.question: Which cellular generation introduced mobile broadband data services?
questions.explanation: 3G (e.g., UMTS) brought usable mobile Internet and video calling.

questions.question: What does PSTN stand for?
questions.explanation: The PSTN is the traditional circuit-switched landline telephone system.

questions.question: What does ISDN stand for?
questions.explanation: ISDN carries digital voice and data over traditional copper telephone lines.

questions.question: What does DSL stand for?
questions.explanation: DSL provides broadband Internet over ordinary telephone copper pairs.

questions.question: What characterizes ADSL compared to SDSL?
questions.explanation: Asymmetric DSL allocates more bandwidth to downloads than uploads.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of optical fiber over copper cabling?
questions.explanation: Fiber uses light pulses, so it is immune to EMI and supports huge bandwidth.

questions.question: At approximately what altitude do GEO satellites orbit?
questions.explanation: Geostationary satellites orbit about 35,786 km above the equator.

questions.question: Which satellite orbit offers the lowest communication latency?
questions.explanation: Low Earth Orbit satellites (160-2,000 km) minimize signal travel delay.

questions.question: What does VoIP stand for?
questions.explanation: VoIP carries telephone calls as data packets over IP networks.

questions.question: What does a codec do in telecommunications?
options: Encodes and decodes signals for transmission
questions.explanation: A coder-decoder digitizes analog voice and compresses it for transport.

questions.question: How does throughput differ from bandwidth?
options: Throughput is the actual achieved rate; bandwidth is the maximum capacity
Bandwidth is measured, throughput is theoretical
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the link's capacity; throughput is the real delivered data rate.

questions.question: What is latency?
questions.explanation: Latency is the time it takes a signal or packet to travel to its destination.

questions.question: What is attenuation?
options: Loss of signal strength over distance
questions.explanation: Attenuation is the gradual weakening of a signal as it travels through a medium.

questions.question: During a traditional telephone call, both people can speak and be heard at the same time. Which duplex mode does this describe?
questions.explanation: A telephone call is full-duplex because voice travels in both directions simultaneously.

questions.question: On a push-to-talk two-way radio, a speaker must release the button before the other party can reply. Which duplex mode is this?
questions.explanation: Push-to-talk radio is half-duplex: the channel carries only one direction at a time.

questions.question: Which cellular generation is built on an all-IP network using LTE?
questions.explanation: 4G LTE replaced circuit switching entirely with packet-switched IP transport.

questions.question: What is a defining capability of 5G networks?
options: Ultra-low latency and massive device density
questions.explanation: 5G targets ~1 ms latency, gigabit speeds, and dense IoT connectivity.

questions.question: A transmitter feeds 100 mW into a cable with 10 dB of loss. What power reaches the far end?
questions.explanation: A 10 dB loss divides power by 10 (10^(-10/10) = 0.1): 100 mW x 0.1 = 10 mW.

questions.question: Using the Nyquist formula, what is the maximum data rate of a noiseless 6 kHz channel using 4 signal levels?
questions.explanation: Nyquist: 2 x B x log2(L) = 2 x 6000 x log2(4) = 12000 x 2 = 24 kbps.

questions.question: A cellular system lets many users share the same frequency band simultaneously, distinguishing calls only by assigned codes. Which multiplexing technique is this?
questions.explanation: CDMA (Code Division Multiple Access) lets all users transmit at once on the same band, separated by unique spreading codes.

questions.question: What is the data rate of the European E1 digital carrier?
questions.explanation: E1 carries 32 x 64 kbps time slots (30 payload channels plus signaling/framing) for a total of 2.048 Mbps.

questions.question: Which theorem states that an analog signal must be sampled at least twice its highest frequency to be reconstructed perfectly?
questions.explanation: The Nyquist sampling theorem requires a sampling rate of at least 2 x fmax; voice at 4 kHz is sampled at 8 kHz.
